action.text: Task: Add regression tests for port access on urlsplit/urlparse results. Tests pass (CHK-0022). Implementation: port property checks isdigit()+isascii(), raises ValueError for non-digit/non-ASCII, then checks 0<=port<=65535. Error at .port access, not construction. Empty/absent port→None. Next: add documentation to Doc/library/urllib.parse.rst with boundary/error doctest examples. Then run public check and submit.

action.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  Port validation is performed
   when the :attr:`port` attribute is accessed, not when the parse result
   is constructed.  The port must be an ASCII decimal integer in the range
   0 through 65535 (inclusive).  If the netloc has no port component or the
   port component is empty, :attr:`port` returns :const:`None`.

   .. doctest::
      :options: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlsplit

      >>> # No port: .port is None
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com/").port is None
      True
      >>> # Empty port (trailing colon, no digits): .port is None
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:/%").port is None
      True

      >>> # Valid boundary ports
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:0/").port
      0
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:65535/").port
      65535

      >>> # Out-of-range port: error at .port access, not at parse time
      >>> p = urlparse("http://example.com:65536/")
      >>> p.netloc
      'example.com:65536'
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535

      >>> # Negative port: minus sign is not a digit
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:-1/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'

      >>> # Non-integer port
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:abc/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'

      >>> # Non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari six, U+0966)
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:\u0966/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as '६'

      >>> # urlsplit has identical port behavior
      >>> urlsplit("http://example.com:65536/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535

   See section :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the
   result object.
